sections.eyebrow: WHAT WHARTON PREPARES YOU TO DO WITH AI
sections.heading: Build with AI. Bring business expertise.
sections.quote: As AI becomes more capable, the deeper question is what we ask of ourselves. A Wharton MBA develops the expertise to recognize what matters, the judgment to question even a convincing answer, and the conviction to take responsibility for a decision no technology can make on our behalf.
sections.role: Vice Dean of the MBA Program
sections.approvalNote: Proposed quote — adapted from interview themes; pending Michael Roberts’ approval.

sections.heading: AI capability starts with understanding the business.
sections.text: Roberts describes Wharton’s approach to preparing students to build solutions with AI: combine knowledge of the technology with business expertise, rethink workflows, and take responsibility for the decisions that follow.

sections.eyebrow: HOW WHARTON’S AI INSIGHTS REACH THE CLASSROOM
sections.heading:
AI Research

sections.text: Wharton faculty study how AI changes business and engage with organizations putting it to work. Roberts describes how research, industry experience, and questions from students inform one another. For MBA prospects, that exchange connects AI learning to the questions businesses are facing.

sections.heading: Study AI with a school investigating its impact.

items.title: When does AI help—and when does it hinder?
items.description: Research by Wharton’s Hamsa Bastani and collaborators examines how access to an AI tutor affects practice and skill development in chess. It offers a concrete example of Wharton studying how AI can support learning.

items.title: How is AI changing the skills businesses need?
items.description: The Wharton–Accenture Skills Index examines the relationship between AI, employer demand, and the value of specific skills. Explore the evidence behind changing expectations for work.

sections.eyebrow: THREE CAPABILITIES FOR WORKING WITH AI
sections.heading: Understand the output. Build the solution. Own the decision.

items.title: Question AI-generated answers
items.description: Use business expertise to examine an AI-generated answer, question its assumptions, and judge whether it solves the problem.

items.title: Build and rethink with AI
items.description: Combine business expertise and AI capability to build practical solutions—and rethink entire workflows with AI in mind.

items.title: Own AI-supported decisions
items.description: Explain how you used AI, communicate the reasoning, and take responsibility for the decision.

sections.heading: Use AI to deepen your thinking.
sections.text: Roberts emphasizes that AI makes business expertise and judgment more important, because stronger models can sound more convincing. Wharton’s MBA AI guidance asks students to use AI to support their own learning and analysis. Application, discussion, and problem-solving remain central to the education Roberts describes.

action.label: Read the MBA’s guidance on AI use

sections.eyebrow: BRINGING AI TOOLS INTO MBA LEARNING
sections.heading: New AI capabilities. Practical access.
sections.text: Wharton backs AI learning with school-supported tools and faculty-led workshops. Roberts describes Codex and Claude Code access for MBA students moving from idea to implementation in about a month, and a practical workshop series created as the technology evolved.

sections.eyebrow: WHAT YOU CAN EXPLORE IN THE WHARTON MBA
sections.heading: AI foundations, tools, and a path to go deeper.

items.title: AI learning from Pre-Term
items.description: AI learning begins during Pre-Term. Wharton also provides MBA students with access to ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, and Claude Code. Students must follow each instructor’s expectations for AI use.

items.title: Faculty-led AI workshops
items.description: In fall 2026, Roberts organized a four-part practical AI workshop series with Ethan Mollick, Kartik Hosanagar, and Daniel Rock, sharing how they use AI in their professional and personal lives.

items.title: A dedicated AI MBA major
items.description: The Artificial Intelligence for Business major combines technical fluency with the business, economic, legal, ethical, psychological, and societal dimensions of AI.

sections.heading: Build an AI idea through experimentation.
sections.text: Wharton profiled Hetvee Marviya, WG’27, building an AI-powered platform that turns current events into personalized comic strips for children. In the Generative AI Studio, students develop their ideas through prototyping, critique, and weekly iteration.

sections.heading: Work with AI beyond the classroom.
sections.text: Wharton’s AI & Analytics Accelerator gives selected students experience with company datasets and business problems. Fall 2026 projects include capturing organizational knowledge for AI agents and evaluating AI-generated travel content. It is another way to explore how AI techniques meet the demands of a business problem.

sections.heading: Learn more about AI at Wharton.
sections.text: Explore Wharton’s schoolwide AI teaching and research, and read the MBA’s guidance on school-supported AI tools. The faculty research, student project, and AI learning opportunities featured here link to their Wharton sources.
